en.title: All Creatures of Our God and King
en.author: Francis of Assisi
stanzas:
[D]All creatures of our [Bm]God and [A]king
[D]Lift up your voice and [Bm]with us [A]sing,
[D]Alle[G]lu[D]ia! [Bm]Alle[A]lu[D]ia!
[D]Thou burning sun with [A7]golden [D]beam,
[D]Thou silver moon with [G]softer [D]gleam!

Thou rushing wind that art so strong
Ye clouds that sail in Heaven along,
O praise Him! Alleluia!
Thou rising moon, in praise rejoice,
Ye lights of evening, find a voice!

Thou flowing water, pure and clear,
Make music for thy Lord to hear,
O praise Him! Alleluia!
Thou fire so masterful and bright,
That givest man both warmth and light.

Dear mother earth, who day by day
Unfoldest blessings on our way,
O praise Him! Alleluia!
The flowers and fruits that in thee grow,
Let them His glory also show.

And all ye men of tender heart,
Forgiving others, take your part,
O sing ye! Alleluia!
Ye who long pain and sorrow bear,
Praise God and on Him cast your care!

And thou most kind and gentle death,
Waiting to hush our latest breath,
O praise Him! Alleluia!
Thou leadest home the child of God,
And Christ our Lord the way hath trod.

Let all things their creator bless,
And worship Him in humbleness,
O praise Him! Alleluia!
Praise, praise the Father, praise the Son,
And praise the Spirit, Three in One!

notes: Text: the Cyber Hymnal's seven stanzas of Draper's 1919 translation, with its refrain lifted into the chorus field -- the Cyber Hymnal prints "Refrain" after every stanza, so the shells' repeat-after-each-stanza behaviour is exactly right. Stanza 1's third line is "Alleluia! Alleluia!" where later stanzas have "O praise Him! Alleluia!" (stanza 5: "O sing ye! Alleluia!"); that variation is in the source and is standard. Hymnary's representative text and Timeless Truths both drop to five stanzas (no "Dear mother earth", no "And thou most kind and gentle death") and read "Thou rising morn" for the Cyber Hymnal's "Thou rising moon"; "moon" is Draper's and is kept. Key D confirmed three ways: the hymnchords.net chart (Trinity Hymnal p.115, transposed there from E-flat), hymnary's incipit database, and Timeless Truths. CHORDS: lines 1-2 share a melody and so share a chart. THE REFRAIN CHART IS MY OWN and is the weakest part of this file -- the published chart moves on nearly every syllable and its PDF text layout could not be aligned to syllables with confidence, so the refrain is best-effort. STRUCTURE: the meter 8.8.4.4.8.8 counts the two Alleluias as separate 4-syllable lines, but every source consulted prints them on one line ("Alleluia! Alleluia!"), so each stanza here is 5 lines, not 6. The chorus adds the 6+12 refrain. VERIFIED 2026-08-02: cross-checked against the LDS hymnal #62 (churchofjesuschrist.org), which carries Draper's wording for the four stanzas it prints, with its own alterations ("Thou rising morn", "That gives to man both warmth and light") -- consistent with the morn/moon remark above; the lowercase "God and king" is genuinely the Cyber Hymnal's printing. Meter re-verified against hymnary's LASST UNS ERFREUEN tune page ("8.8.4.4.8.8 with refrain", representative score in D).
